comment: A REFUSAL'S CODE (SDK 0.14.4; inapp-platform-contract.md, 'A refusal's code'). One rule on every SDK — iOS, Android, Kotlin Multiplatform (through them), Flutter, React Native and the website loader — run against these vectors by each. A non-2xx answer whose JSON body carries a non-blank string `code` keeps that code (trimmed), known to the SDK or not. Otherwise the status decides: 400 and 422 → invalid_request; 401 → invalid_key; 403 → origin_refused; 404 → not_found; 429 → rate_limited; 502, 503, 504 and 520–524 → unavailable (a gateway that could not reach Graine or gave up waiting, Graine itself down, and the same answers from the CDN in front of it — worth trying again later); every other status → unknown. An SDK whose unknown code carries a word carries `http_<status>` (`raw` below: iOS .unknown("http_500"), Android Unknown("http_500")); the others say `unknown`. No answer at all is `network`, never a status. `name` says why the vector is here.
